newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle feedlots quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle feedlots quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Friday were quiet, with no sales expected following Thursday's active trade, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of this week's showlist sold at $65.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week.
Light bids at $64.00 were passed by owners Friday morning, who priced cattle at $65.00-$66.00, sources said.

Most showlists was "cleaned-up" in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said. Kansas sources said some cattle could be carried over into next week, but they were unfinished and could use more days on feed.

Cattle feeders said this afternoon's USDA monthly Cattle on Feed Report could have a psychological impact on next week's fed cattle prices, especially if the market perceives a dramatic increase in future cattle supplies.
Estimates in a Reuters survey of analysts, for on-feed supplies in the seven key states as of January 1 averaged 104.2 percent in a range of 102 to 105 percent of a year ago.
December placement estimates averaged 108.2 percent in a range of 103 to 112 percent and marketings estimates averaged 101.8 in a range of 99 to 107.1 percent of last year.
